prompt: What is the main purpose of a sentinel node in a linked list implementation?
explanation: A sentinel provides a permanent dummy head/tail so every real node always has a valid neighbor, removing the need to special-case empty lists or boundaries.

prompt: Removing duplicates from an unsorted singly-linked list of n elements, using only O(1) extra memory (no hash set or auxiliary list) and no recursion -- what is the achievable worst-case time complexity?
explanation: Without extra memory to track 'seen' values, each of the n elements must be checked against every element still ahead of it in the list -- worst case (n-1)+(n-2)+...+1 = Theta(n^2) total operations.
